arxiv-2107-06084.title: Decentralized LTL Enforcement
arxiv-2107-06084.creator: Florian Gallay Yliès Falcone
arxiv-2107-06084.description: Abstract We consider the runtime enforcement of Linear-time Temporal Logic formulas on decentralized systems with no central observation point nor authority. A so-called enforcer is attached to each system component and observes its local trace. Should the global trace violate the specification, the enforcers coordinate to correct their local traces.

arxiv-2303-06051.title: NFT Bubbles
arxiv-2303-06051.creator: Andrea Barbon, Angelo Ranaldo
arxiv-2303-06051.description: Abstract By investigating nonfungible tokens (NFTs), we provide the first systematic study of retail investor behavior through asset bubbles. Given that NFTs are recorded in public blockchains, we are able to track investor behavior over time, leading to the identification of numerous price run-ups and crashes.

arxiv-2310-16722.title: Assessing the Suitability of the Langevin Equation for Analyzing Measured Data Through Downsampling Journal: \JSTAT
arxiv-2310-16722.creator: Pyei Phyo Lin, Matthias Wächter, Joachim Peinke, M. Reza Rahimi Tabar
arxiv-2310-16722.description: Abstract The measured time series from complex systems are renowned for their intricate stochastic behavior, characterized by random fluctuations stemming from external influences and nonlinear interactions. These fluctuations take diverse forms, ranging from continuous trajectories reminiscent of Brownian motion to noncontinuous trajectories featuring jump events.

arxiv-2406-01298.title: Floquet engineering nearly flat bands through quantum-geometric light-matter coupling with surface polaritons
arxiv-2406-01298.creator: Mikołaj Walicki, Christian J. Eckhardt, Michael A. Sentef
arxiv-2406-01298.description: Abstract We investigate Floquet engineering in a sawtooth chain – a minimal model hosting a nearly flat band endowed with nontrivial quantum geometry – coupled to driven surface polaritons. In this paradigmatic flat band model, light-matter coupling to a flat band is enabled by quantum geometry despite the vanishing band velocity and band curvature.

arxiv-2509-23300.title: Entanglement signatures of gapless topological phases in a p p -wave superconductor
arxiv-2509-23300.creator: S. Srinidhi ID, Shashi C. L. Srivastava ID, Jayendra N. Bandyopadhyay ID
arxiv-2509-23300.description: Abstract We explore the gapless topological phases of a p p -wave superconductor, probing its rich topologically ordered phases and underlying quantum phenomena. The topological order of the system is characterized by studying its entanglement properties. This study confirms the bulk-boundary correspondence in the entanglement spectrum, even without a full bulk gap.

arxiv-2511-07279.title: From Fresh to Salty: How Ions Modulate Solvent-Mediated Interactions between Grafted Silica Nanoparticles in Water
arxiv-2511-07279.creator: Yuvraj Singh, Chandan K. Choudhury, Rakesh S. Singh
arxiv-2511-07279.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuvraj Singh, Chandan K. Choudhury, Rakesh S. Singh. Nanoparticles (NPs) are fundamental building blocks for engineering functional soft materials, where precise control over the solvent-mediated inter-particle effective interaction ( U eff U_{\rm eff} ) is essential for tailoring bulk structure and properties. These solvent-mediated interactions are strongly influenced by NP’s surface chemistry, solvent properties, and thermodynamic conditions such as temperature ( T T ) and pressure ( P P ).

pmc-10542351.title: A study on improving the prediction accuracy of cold forging die life based on quantitative evaluation of phosphate film damage
pmc-10542351.creator: Young Ho Seo
pmc-10542351.description: In designing the multi-stage cold forging process, an important factor along with formability is the die life cycle. As the die life cycle is closely related to the integrity of the phosphate film coating on the surface of the material, this study presents a method for predicting the die life cycle considering damage to the phosphate film coating.

pmc-10691408.title: Wet chemical synthesis of TGA capped Ag2S nanoparticles and their use for fluorescence imaging and temperature sensing in living cells†
pmc-10691408.creator: Mayssa Ibrahim, P. Camarero, Liyan Ming, Mohamed Haouari, Noura Amamou, P. Haro-González, Fredj Hassen
pmc-10691408.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In this work, we describe a simple wet chemical route for preparing silver sulfide nanoparticles (Ag2S) encapsulated with thioglycolic acid (TGA). By using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), energy dispersive X-ray (EDS) microanalysis, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and dynamic light scattering (DLS), we have found that these nanoparticles were enrobed by TGA molecules and they have an Ag/S ratio nearly equal to 2.2 and a nearly spherical shape with two average size populations.

pmc-11496709.title: A rapid-convergent particle swarm optimization approach for multiscale design of high-permeance seawater reverse osmosis systems
pmc-11496709.creator: Ke Chen, Jiu Luo, Junzhi Chen, Yutong Lu, Yi Heng
pmc-11496709.description: Directly solving sophisticated partial differential equation constrained optimization problems is not only extremely time-consuming, but also very hard to find unique optimal solutions. Here, we propose stable and efficient surrogate models for seawater reverse osmosis desalination processes that enable thorough quantitative description of hydrodynamics and local transport characteristics in narrow flow channels.

pmc-12830885.title: Global coral genomic vulnerability explains recent reef losses
pmc-12830885.creator: Oliver Selmoni, Phillip A Cleves, Moises Exposito-Alonso
pmc-12830885.description: The dramatic decline of reef-building corals calls for a better understanding of coral adaptation to ocean warming. Here, we characterize genetic diversity of the widespread genus Acropora by building a genomic database of 595 coral samples from different oceanic regions—from the Great Barrier Reef to the Persian Gulf.

pmc-13362644.title: Association Between Female Reproductive Factors and Laryngopharyngeal Reflux: A National Population-Based Study
pmc-13362644.creator: Kyung Hoon Park, Jung Ho Park, Hong Kyu Lee, Mi Jung Kwon, Heejin Kim, Jeong Wook Kang
pmc-13362644.description: Background: The association between female reproductive factors and laryngopharyngeal reflux (LPR) remains poorly understood. This study investigated the relationship between reproductive history and LPR risk in women using a large nationally representative cohort. Methods: We conducted a nested case–control study using linked data from the Korean National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey and the National Health Insurance Service database (2007–2017).

pmc-13536694.title: Molecular PET imaging of integrin αvβ6 reveals biliary and fibrotic changes in preclinical MASH
pmc-13536694.creator: Xiaoyi Wang, Mengqi Wang, Pengzhe Han, Huanhuan Song, Xuchen Zhao, Nannan Chen, Congzhong Hu, Xueqin Liu, Xiaolong Li, Xifeng Fu, Steven Liang, Zhifang Wu, Yanzhang Tian, Tuo Shao
pmc-13536694.description: BackgroundThe progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) involves complex crosstalk among hepatocellular injury, inflammation, and ductular reaction—a process characterized by biliary epithelial proliferation and fibrotic activation. Integrin αvβ6, an epithelial-specific receptor largely absent in normal liver but induced under chronic injury, plays a pivotal role in activating latent TGF-β and driving fibrogenesis.

pmc-13655397.title: Cadherin-26 Promotes Airway Remodeling via Stabilizing Epithelial Expression of the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor in Asthma
pmc-13655397.creator: Jiali Gao, Gongqi Chen, Chunli Huang, Zhen Wang, Wei Gu, Huiru Jie, Tiantian Xiong, Yuchen Feng, Lingling Yi, Dan Cheng, Guohua Zhen
pmc-13655397.description: PurposeActivation of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling in airway epithelial cells leads to epithelial-mesenchymal transformation (EMT) and airway remodeling in asthma. However, the mechanism regulating EGFR expression is not fully understood. We hypothesized that cadherin-26 (CDH26), a highly expressed cadherin in airway epithelium, promotes airway remodeling via regulating EGFR signaling in asthma.
